summary: @container applies styles based on the width of the element's container instead of the whole screen. Mark a parent with container-type: inline-size, then write @container (min-width: ...) rules for its children.
notes: In the preview, main is about 395px wide, so (min-width: 300px) is true and its card is a row. The aside is about 195px wide, so its card stays stacked.
A media query could not do this: both cards are on the same screen, at the same screen width.
If the whole page gets narrow enough that main is under 300px, its card stacks too.
pitfall: Setting container-type on the card itself and querying it from the card's own rule. An element cannot respond to its own size; the container must be an ancestor.
